title: Sobolev realization of an elliptic operator has closed range
statement: All vector spaces are over the real field $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth Riemannian metric and volume form. Let $G,H$ be smooth real vector bundles of the same finite rank, with smooth positive definite fibre metrics. Let $Q:\Gamma^\infty(G)\to\Gamma^\infty(H)$ be a real-linear differential operator with smooth coefficients of order at most $k\geq1$, locally $Q=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq k}b_\alpha(x)\partial^\alpha$, whose degree-$k$ principal symbol $\sum_{|\alpha|=k}b_\alpha(x)\xi^\alpha:G_x\to H_x$ is invertible for every nonzero real cotangent vector $\xi$. For a metric bundle $B$, let $L^2(B)$ be the Hilbert completion of its smooth sections in the norm $\|u\|_0^2=\int_N|u|^2\,dV$. This completion canonically identifies with measurable square-integrable sections modulo almost-everywhere equality. Let $H^k(B)$ be their Sobolev completion: choose a finite smooth trivializing atlas and subordinate smooth partition of unity, take in each chart the Euclidean $L^2$ norms of all derivatives of the localized section through order $k$, and sum their squares. These completions admit the canonical injective maps $H^k(B)\hookrightarrow L^2(B)\hookrightarrow\mathcal D^{\prime}(B)$, where $\mathcal D^{\prime}(B)$ denotes distributional sections (local distributions in smooth frames, with the usual change-of-frame rule); smooth sections have their usual image under these maps. In particular $L^2(B)$ is a complete real inner product space for the integrated pairing. The map $Q$ extends uniquely to a bounded real-linear operator $T_Q:H^k(G)\to L^2(H)$, its value $T_Qu$ agrees with $Qu$ computed by distributional differentiation in charts, and its range is closed in $L^2(H)$.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §1 (1.4), VI §2 Sobolev spaces and the closed-Sobolev-range part of Corollary (2.4)(ii), equations (2.5)--(2.6), printed pp.288--290; the local-system argument applies between two metric bundles; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-bundle-sobolev-rellich] to $B=G$ and $B=H$, with $s=k$. It gives precisely the asserted measurable realization, Hilbert structures, and injective maps into $L^2$ and distributions. In particular $E=H^k(G)$ is Hilbert, $F=L^2(H)$ is complete, and $J:E\to L^2(G)$ is bounded and compact. Smooth sections have their original distributional images.

Choose the finite atlas to trivialize both bundles, refining the given one if necessary; the Sobolev realization lemma gives equivalent norms after this change, so a bound for the refined norm yields a bound for the original norm. Write $u=\sum_i\chi_i u$. In the $i$th chart $Q(\chi_i u)=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq k}b_{i,\alpha}\partial^\alpha(\chi_i u)$. On the compact support of $\chi_i$, each coefficient and the volume/metric comparison factors are bounded. The triangle inequality gives $\|Qu\|_{L^2(H)}\leq\sum_{i,\alpha}M_{i,\alpha}\|\partial^\alpha(\chi_i u)\|_2\leq M\|u\|_{H^k(G)}$, taking $M>0$ larger than the sum of these finitely many constants. Regard smooth sections as a dense linear subspace of $E$. Apply [lem-sfb-dense-subspace-contractive-extension] over $\mathbf R$ to $Q/M$ and multiply the extension by $M$. This constructs a unique bounded linear extension $T_Q:E\to F$.

source.place: VI §1 local formula (1.1), VI §2 Sobolev setup; explicit finite-chart estimate by NU

proof.text: For $u\in E$, take smooth $u_n\to u$ in $H^k$. By [lem-sfb-bundle-sobolev-rellich], every localized derivative through order $k$ converges in $L^2$ to the corresponding distributional derivative of $u$. Multiplication by the bounded local coefficients preserves this convergence. Thus the local differential expressions $Qu_n$ converge to the distributional $Qu$, whereas the bounded extension gives $Qu_n\to T_Qu$ in $L^2(H)$. These limits agree as distributions: pairing an $L^2$ difference with a compactly supported smooth test section is bounded by its $L^2$ norm times the test section's $L^2$ norm. The injectivity into distributions identifies their values. This proves the asserted agreement.

source.place: VI §2 distributional extension in (2.3); explicit limiting argument by NU

proof.text: For smooth $u_n$, [lem-sfb-elliptic-global-garding-estimate] gives $\|u_n\|_E\leq C(\|Qu_n\|_F+\|u_n\|_{L^2(G)})$. Let $u_n\to u$ in $E$; the boundedness of $T_Q$ and $J$ and continuity of norms give $\|u\|_E\leq C(\|T_Qu\|_F+\|Ju\|_{L^2(G)})$ for all $u\in E$. Therefore [lem-sfb-compact-remainder-coercivity], applied to $T=T_Q$ and this compact $J$, supplies $D>0$ with $\|v\|_E\leq D\|T_Qv\|_F$ on $K^\perp$, where $K=\ker T_Q$ and orthogonality is for the $H^k$ inner product.

source.place: VI §2 (2.3) and compactness argument in Corollary (2.4)(ii); kernel-complement formulation by NU

proof.text: Let $y_n=T_Qx_n\to y$ in $F$. The subspace $K$ is closed since $T_Q$ is continuous. By [lem-sfb-hilbert-orthogonal-projection], write $x_n=z_n+v_n$ with $z_n\in K$ and $v_n\in K^\perp$. Then $T_Qv_n=y_n$. Applying the estimate of the preceding step to $v_n-v_l\in K^\perp$ gives $\|v_n-v_l\|_E\leq D\|y_n-y_l\|_F$. Hence $(v_n)$ is Cauchy, so it converges to some $v\in E$. Continuity gives $T_Qv=y$. Thus every convergent sequence in the range has its limit in the range, which is the closedness criterion in the norm metric on $F$.

source.place: VI §2 Corollary (2.4)(ii), closedness after the estimate; explicit Cauchy argument by NU

proof_origin.place: Demailly VI §2 (2.2), (2.3), proof of (2.4)(ii), read online; NU supplies the finite-chart extension argument and uses the equivalent kernel-complement compactness argument.
